subject: Strategic cost equalization & technical carveout for TeamQOps
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@teamqops.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@teamqops.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor swap / pricing parity request

Vanessa —

Thanks for taking this. Quick context: TeamQOps is evaluating a vendor swap for inference (current vendor: Infratek). Their incumbent has offered a commercial reset with a 28% list discount if we commit to a 12-month reserved pool, plus a $150k migration credit tied to pilot completion. We like Redwood's latency and the unified runtime story, but procurement needs parity (or a clearly superior package) to justify the disruption.

Key numbers from our side (monthly avg last 6 months):
- Token throughput: ~1.8B tokens / month
- Peak concurrent requests: ~240 requests/sec
- Mix: 75% streaming chat, 25% batch embeddings

What we need from you to move fast:
1) Is Redwood able to match or beat the incumbent's effective price for a committed 12-month reserved pool?
2) Can you offer a migration credit or onboarding stipend tied to pilot metrics?
3) Any technical carveouts we should be aware of (model variants, quantization compatibility, KV cache behavior) that would affect live parity?

Procurement timeline: decision window opens Apr 15; target to sign by Apr 30.

Appreciate a concise proposal. If helpful, I can share a redacted invoice/usage slice.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Cloud Ops, TeamQ Operations
procurement@teamqops.com

Attachment: TeamQOps_cost_snapshot_Q1_2027.csv (attached by Samir)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@teamqops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor swap / pricing parity request

Samir —

Thanks for the clear context and the numbers. High level answer: yes — we can put together a matched economics package, with a technical carveout that reduces your operational risk during cutover. Below is a concise proposal you can take to procurement today. I'll follow up with a short term sheet if this looks directionally right.

Proposal options (committed 12 months):
A) Reserved Dedicated Pool (recommended for predictability)
  - Commit: 40 reserved GPUs (NVIDIA H100-equivalent)
  - Economics: 30% list discount off standard reserved price; additional 5% volume kicker if monthly tokens > 2.0B for any two months in a row
  - Onboarding credit: $125k credit applied to first invoice upon successful pilot signoff (pilot metrics: <100ms median response for 512-token prompts; KV cold-start <1s)
  - Technical carveout: model variant parity guaranteed for Redwood-curated families (LLM-v1/v2). For third-party forks we list exceptions in the runbook.

B) Hosted API + Reserved Buffer (lower ops overhead)
  - No GPU commit required; usage-pricing with committed monthly minimum (equivalent annualized spend)
  - Effective discount: ~22% on equivalent token spend at your volumes
  - Onboarding credit: $75k pilot credit

Notes / tradeoffs:
- Migration credit is conditional on a 4-week pilot demonstrating parity on a representative 100k-message prompt set; we can accept an incumbent baseline trace for apples-to-apples comparison.
- The reserved pool option gives you the simplest unit economics and an SLA uplift; Hosted + Buffer is faster to stand up but marginally higher unit cost.
- Quantization/compatibility: the main friction we see is custom operator layers in some in-house fine-tuned variants. Connor (cc'd) will validate specific models; most customers achieve parity with standard conversion/quantization within a 2–3 week engineering window.

Attachments: redwood-deal-summary-20270405.xlsx (pricing sheet), TQOps_RFP_response_v2.pdf (scope & runbook excerpt)

If that directionally matches, I'll ask Marissa to draft a short term sheet (financials only) and Connor to prepare a migration checklist. Can you confirm the list token numbers and whether the pilot can start by Apr 12?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference runtime and tooling
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@teamqops.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor swap / pricing parity request

Samir / Vanessa —

Quick technical readout and migration checklist (summary):

1) Model compatibility baseline
  - If your workload uses standard transformer-based families (no custom CUDA ops), conversion is straightforward; we'll run an automated validation harness we call the "runtime parity check".
  - For custom ops / fused kernels, we'll either provide a binary-compatible runtime path or a documented deviation with performance impact estimates.

2) KV cache & streaming behavior
  - Redwood's KV cache semantics match common open runtimes; however, large persistent prompt prefixes need explicit warmup. We recommend a 48-hour warmup period during pilot.
  - Streaming latency SLOs are achievable with our continuous batching config; we'll surface batching headroom in the pilot report.

3) Migration tasks & timeline (pilot->prod):
  - Week 0: run parity harness on a 10k-prompt sample (2–3 days)
  - Week 1: scoped pilot with a shadowed traffic slice (1 week)
  - Week 2–3: performance tuning and quantization pass
  - Week 4: go/no-go and credit signoff

4) Operational handoffs
  - We'll supply runbook artifacts (incident playbooks, tracing hooks, rollout rollback scripts). Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-teamqops-migration-runbook

I'll work with your infra engineer during Week 0 to capture any variant-level blockers. Marissa — please include a note in the term sheet about the $125k credit conditional on pilot metrics; I mapped out the acceptance tests in the attached runbook excerpt.

Connor O'Brien
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0127
